machine: Apple M1, 16 GiB RAM, macOS 26.6.2 arm64; shared host, no CPU affinity.
build: CMake 4.1.1; Apple clang 21.0.0; Release -O3 -DNDEBUG -arch arm64; no fast-math. Native target standards: C++23 for SOTS/DP/SQUISH, C++17 for DOTS. Julia 1.12.6 / FrechetDist 2.1.0. Baseline revision ce40df79a77db8eb4bb31d7316a187c07b2ad921. Full source and binary hashes accompany the JSON evidence.
profile: Instruments Time Profiler 27.0: ten seconds, 9,872 samples, one main thread. ID 21 (588 input points), ε=0.1 and δ=272.727272727273; repeated simplification warms the existing grid-shape caches.
Edge cropping and its inline helpers account for 7,216 samples (73.1%); tangent selection accounts for 623 (6.3%). These sampled leaf-frame counts are preserved in profile-before.json.

A separate cold CLI phase-timer run attributes 78.7% to intersection: 68,296 intersection calls and 72,914 wedge updates. Fréchet checking is absent from the timed core. Phase timers are explanatory evidence, never benchmark samples.
optimizations: Evaluated separately (follow-up PR-B, not in this harness-only checkout — current simplify_geometry.h de7613aac3c553f97a9b3bcf8bea4bca3bb84105c58f80e1043d87d3faf9c7e0 identical to base 34cf5bb without batching; historical batch cb9f12bb274dc5d0a3660926f408e9179585fe8f61c054af666697d3d3abe2e5): test four independent vertices at a time in the already-inside prefix of each clip edge. This reduces branching and exposes determinant arithmetic to vectorization. A block containing an outside vertex resumes the original scalar path.

Preserved in that separate evaluation: intersection formulas, edge order, vertex order, anchor tie order and floating-point flags. No new threads or trajectory-sized caches. The independent scalar clipping oracle agreed bit for bit on all boundary patterns through ten vertices plus 20,000 random rings (validated separately, not in this checkout).

The 200-case rerun checked byte-identical curves and exactly equal continuous Fréchet distances before/after. Baseline binaries, controls and outputs were frozen. Each phase stored ten raw samples per cell; original SOTS was also rerun within final shuffled rounds. Results are retained as historical evidence; this checkout's build (see build.json) has identical before/after hashes with no batching.
conclusion: Local M1 (shared host) observed 1.115× vs paired reference (13.4604 vs 15.0092 ms, initial 18.0642 ms) on the separately evaluated batch (cb9f12bb274, not in this checkout), but CI (Ubuntu 24.04 g++-14, 20 configs ×10 IDs, 10 runs Welch 95%) shows mean 1.00× (neutral, 0% cut, 20/20 passed, per-config 0.94–1.08×; intersect 1.07× but overall neutral, Run 36460949757). Corrected claim is neutral, not 10.3%.

Performance parity is not achieved. On final case-balanced means SOTS still takes 69.9× DOTS time, 335.6× SQUISH time, and 776.1× DP time (local M1; CI shows similar gaps). Different point counts and actual errors remain visible; these ratios compare a common verified upper bound, not identical outputs across algorithms.

Next priority: prove anchor dominance or equivalent-state elimination to reduce polygon updates while preserving longest-stab and last-anchor tie behavior. Then investigate incremental convex clipping and a structure-of-arrays SIMD layout for longer rings. Each needs differential correctness checks; simply reducing anchors changes the algorithm.

Caching Fréchet results cannot improve core_ms because verification is already outside timing. Grid shapes and clip buffers are already cached within each process. Fine-ε work dominates the aggregate; inspect each tier and its deviations before generalizing to another workload.
